subject: Clarifying anonymity of logs and BAA scope for transient PHI
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medicus-analytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hastings <tom.hastings@bluebridge.io>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: pseudonymized patient identifiers in logs — BAA implication

Hi Neha,

Quick background: we ingest NLP outputs from Redwood for a line-of-business app. Our security team found that the request/response logs in our staging account include short-lived pseudonyms (e.g., patient_47a9) that map back to patient IDs in our EHR during enrichment. We treat that mapping as sensitive.

Questions:
- From Redwood's perspective, does storing those pseudonyms in logs qualify as PHI under HIPAA if the mapping is only present on our side and the pseudonym token cannot be dereferenced by Redwood?
- If logs do contain reversible tokens, would Redwood require a Dedicated or Private deployment (or a signed BAA) for processing?

Can you point us to any prior evidence or a short statement we can include in our procurement packet? If helpful, I've attached a tiny redacted log sample.

Thanks,
Karen Liu
InfoSec Manager, Medicus Analytics
[Attachment: log_sample_pseudonymized.json (JSON, 8 KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medicus-analytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: pseudonymized patient identifiers in logs — BAA implication

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear note and sample. Looping in Dev (infra/runtime) and Evelyn (product/regulatory) so we can give a short, actionable answer.

High level: Redwood does not have access to mappings you maintain solely on your side. A few bullets we will confirm with Dev:
- Whether our hosted logging includes any request metadata that could be correlated back to your internal mapping (session IDs, customer-provided ids).
- Options to mask or redact those fields in outgoing logs or to disable request body retention for your tenant.
- When we typically recommend Dedicated/Private deployments vs hosted API + BAA.

Attaching our SOC 2 excerpt that covers logging/retention controls for your packet. Will follow up within 24 hours with the technical clarification.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Sales (Privacy & Compliance), Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_soc2_excerpts.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@medicus-analytics.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: pseudonymized patient identifiers in logs — BAA implication

Karen, Neha,

Context from infra: the hosted runtime retains request/response payloads in our short-term operational logs for up to 7 days by default. Those payloads include the raw request body and response tokens if a customer does not enable masking.

Important points:
- If your pseudonym is purely customer-side (a string that only your systems can map), and you ensure the mapping table never leaves your environment, Redwood cannot reasonably "re-identify" from that pseudonym alone. That would generally not be treated as PHI on our side.
- If the pseudonym can be linked via any field that Redwood can access (e.g., you pass the EHR patient id in a header or metadata field), then logs become reversible and we'd treat it as PHI.

Mitigations we can offer on hosted:
- Disable request body retention for your tenant (logs kept only for operational errors, redacted).
- Auto-redaction rules to strip or hash specific JSON fields before they enter our logs.
- A short-term dedicated ingest path (logical isolation within hosted) with stricter retention and audit logs.

For customers who require contractual PHI handling (Delineated by your legal/compliance), we recommend either: a BAA in combination with hosted with agreed retention/redaction controls, or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where customer retains mappings entirely.

I can provide a technical spec for the redaction rules and an example config.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: log_masking_config_example.txt (TXT, 2 KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medicus-analytics.com>
Cc: Tom Hastings <tom.hastings@bluebridge.io>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: pseudonymized patient identifiers in logs — BAA implication

Karen — summarizing next steps so your procurement/compliance teams have what they need:

Action items for Redwood (we will deliver):
- A short technical statement that reversible mappings (i.e., any identifier you also send to Redwood or that exists in headers we retain) will be treated as potential PHI and must be covered by a BAA or prevented by redaction. (Deliverable: 1-pg PDF)
- Example redaction config and a sample of how logs look with fields masked. (Deliverable: config + masked sample)
- If you prefer contractual isolation, we'll share the BAA template and operational differences for Hosted + BAA vs Dedicated/Private. (Deliverable: BAA template + comparison table)

Could you confirm if your mapping table is ever sent to Redwood or included in headers/metadata? Also, does your procurement team prefer a formal BAA before POC or to proceed with hosted + technical controls and sign BAA prior to production?

I'll follow up with the documents this afternoon and include a short note the security team can use in their risk register.

Thanks,
Neha

[Attachment: baa_template_v2.docx (DOCX, 45 KB)]

We will run the POC on hosted if you can: (a) provide the 1-pg technical statement for our packet, (b) the redaction config (we will try that first), and (c) the BAA template for our counsel to review; we'll aim to sign the BAA before production cutover.

Tom — can you confirm whether the redaction approach satisfies our internal control baseline or whether we escalate to Dedicated?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Karen
